A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
diffusion is a social process, and that the diffusion of public heath innovations is influenced by many factors in the social and physical environment.

we have identified the D.A.R.R.E program as an example of a public health innovation that has diffused widely in spite of a lack of evidence of effectiveness, and the syringe exchange program as an example that has diffused slowly despite evidence of effectiveness.

The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no one-size-fits-all solution for the diffusion of public-health innovations.
the diffusion of a public health innovation is not necessarily a good proxy for the effectiveness of the innovation.
there is no single answer to the question of why some public health innovations are diffused and others are not.
